newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: WORK-FOR-DOLE NOT SLAVE LABOUR: HOWARD
The Prime Minister says the Government's new work-for the-dole scheme will not be slave labour or scab labour.
Mr Howard says those participating in the scheme will be paid award rates.
He says that means they'll have to work 15 or 20 hours a week in most cases, and will still have time to look for long term employment.
But Mr Howard has warned young people will lose the right to their unemployment benefits if they refuse to participate in the scheme.
ENVIRONMENTAL JOBS AN OPTION FOR WORK-FOR-THE-DOLE
The Federal Government will consider using work-for-the-dole participants for environmental restoration work.
Environment minister Robert Hill says there is a lot of work to be done in environmental health and work-for-the-dole would be a parallel scheme to the Green Corps.
He says the job opportunities are still a little way into the future.
The Prime Minister announced yesterday the Government would set up pilot schemes in rural and regional areas to make people between 16 and 20 work at award rates for their unemployment benefits.
MIGRANT NUMBERS BEING CAPPED
The Federal Government is moving to cap migrant numbers to ensure its immigration target for this year isn't exceeded.
Immigration Minister, Phillip Ruddock, says the number of available visas in some immigration categories will be reached in a number of weeks.
Mr Ruddock says once these visas are issued, no further visas will be granted until further places become available next financial year.
The categories facing caps include family and fiance programs.
The Government has set a limit of 74-thousand immigrants for this financial year.
GOVERNOR GENERAL SAYS YOUTH UNEMPLOYMENT MAIN PROBLEM
The Governor-General, Sir William Deane, has told a welfare conference that youth unemployment is the major problem facing Australia.
Speaking at the first "Mission Australia" conference, at the Australian National University, Sir William said youth unemployment marginalised a significant proportion of young Australians.
He says it was not only a problem for governments, but for private employers both large and small.
Sir William says consideration of people and their lives must be taken into account in discussions of the economy.
ATTORNEY GENERAL DEFENDS LEGAL AID CUTA
The Federal Government looks set to go ahead with its cuts to legal aid funding despite appeals from the states for a change of mind.
The Federal Attorney General, Daryl Williams, says he won't ask Cabinet to reverse last year's budget decision.

The Prime Minister, John Howard, says the cuts are based on the principle that the Federal Government pays legal aid for cases that come under Commonwealth law and expects the states to pay for state cases.
He says that's fair and sustainable.
GUN COLLECTION MANAGER SACKED
The head of the agency running gun collection in Victoria says the image of the process has been tarnished by an official re-selling surrendered firearms.
The manager of a Ballarat gun collection centre, former police inspector Harry Flynn, has been sacked, after he admitted trading surrended firearms.
Director of the Firearms Reform and Compensation Project, Karen Cleave, says the guns resold were legal.
But she says the project needs to maintain a clean image in which the community can see guns being crushed in every collection centre, and not have some of them diverted.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
